text:
evan: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime section. A few customers asked for a clear statement on "safe defaults" vs opt-in perf knobs. Can we summarize here?

anya: We should boil it down to 3 lines: safe defaults (conservative quant + small batcher waits), opt-in perf (aggressive quant + dynamic batching), and escape hatches (per-route flags + per-customer caps).

lia: For customers worried about regressions, is the canary policy going to include both latency and numeric parity gates?

samir: Yes 100. Canary gates = health checks + p99 latency delta < 5ms + numeric parity regression rate < 0.5% on our eval set. If any gate fails -> auto rollback.

daria: Who owns the parity eval set? We need a curated set per customer vertical (conv, search, code).

samir: Research will own canonical evals; we'll let solutions engineering add tenant-specific evals as needed. Action: Research to publish eval mapping doc.

evan: Customers also care about observability. What signals will we surface in the Console for kernel changes?

samir: Plan: new "kernel" tab on per-route dashboard with: sampled kernel exec time, fallback counts (e.g., flash->fallback), microbatch size histogram, and quantization usage rate.

lia: Can we add a short tooltip that says recommended action when fallback count spikes? E.g., pin to kernel v3 or change quant config.

samir: Good idea. We'll add tooltip text + quick link to rollback playbook.

daria: Small config proposal snippet for product docs so PMs can read it quickly:

```yaml
route_defaults:
  quant_mode: conservative  # conservative|aggressive
  batcher:
    enabled: true
    max_wait_ms: 10
    max_batch_tokens: 1024
  cache_ttl_ms: 300000
  cache_max_bytes_per_customer: 1073741824
```

evan: Nice. Can we also have an automatic "latency_hint" bypass? Some customers want to tag critical calls.

samir: Sidecar will honor `latency_hint: low` and bypass batching. We'll document the cost implications.

anya: Risk callout: aggressive quant -> small accuracy regressions for certain rare tokens. Must require a signed opt-in from large customers.

daria: Also note: kernel v4 has an experimental attention fallback that reduces memory but triggers more fallbacks on Turing-era GPUs. We should flag that in release notes.

samir: Noted. We'll add a "known issues" section for v4 canary.

ops-bot: canary-check: kernel-v4 -> deployed to pool-canary-7; health: 3/3; parity-sample: 0.2% regression (within gate).

evan: Great. Final ask: can someone make a 1-slide summary for PMs and CSMs with defaults + what to tell customers?

lia: I'll draft the slide and share a link by EOD Monday.

anya: Action list: Samir -> runtime RFC + canary gates (due Fri). Lia -> PM slide (EOD Mon). Research -> eval mapping doc (next Wed). Daria -> note for release notes (inline in PR). Thanks all.

evan: Thanks folks :thumbsup:
